solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Applaud attempt lined with crinkly paper for fudge?

indicators.note: crinkled paper is creased out of its flat shape, so the word's letters are crumpled into a new order

parts.note: to applaud is to clap

indicators.note: a garment lined with something has it on the inside, so the attempt word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: an attempt is a try
the five letters of paper, crinkled

explanation.surface: Someone claps a person trying to wrap something in crinkly paper, perhaps a sweet called fudge.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY is split round the crinkled paper: T-RAPPE-RY. 'Fudge' looks like the sweet, but here it is the verb or exclamation meaning nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrappery is empty, insincere talk, the kind of evasive nonsense one calls fudge.

clue.text: It copies a cuckoo clock, barb mostly wide, fluttering (12, two words)

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
something fluttering flaps about restlessly, so the gathered letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
wide with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A description of a cuckoo clock with a barbed decoration flapping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' applies to wide, not barb. The cuckoo clock in the surface is a decoy: the fodder is clock, barb and wid.
explanation.definitionFit: The cow blackbird, or cowbird, is a parasitic American bird that lays its eggs in other birds' nests, just as the cuckoo does.

clue.text: Like a flower family, gold family, in grip of parasitic insect, tailless

indicators.note: with no tail, the insect's name loses its final letter
being in someone's grip means being held inside, so the insect wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a louse, with its last letter docked
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a race is a line of descent, a family

explanation.surface: A botanical note: some flower family, golden-hued, is gripped by a parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauraceous describes plants of the Lauraceae, the laurel family of flowering plants.

clue.text: Tractarian, certainly well-informed, on the rise

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters come backwards

parts.note: certainly as an affirmative reply
to be up on a subject is to be well-informed about it

explanation.surface: A Victorian churchman who was certainly knowledgeable and gaining in influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Bouverie Pusey was a leader of the Oxford Movement, whose members wrote the Tracts for the Times and so were called Tractarians.

clue.text: Alternative to me cutting wood, do they help in laying bridge foundations?

definitions.text: do they help in laying bridge foundations?

indicators.note: something cutting into a thing goes inside it, so the note is set within the word for wood

parts.note: a wood is a stand of trees
mi is the other spelling of the sol-fa note me

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether workers cutting timber, rather than the speaker, help build bridge foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: The third note of the sol-fa scale is spelt both me and mi.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremie is a large funnel and pipe through which concrete is poured under water, as when setting the piers of a bridge.

clue.text: Turmoil coming up about second-class sets of lights in Durban

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
about means surrounding, so the turmoil word goes round the grade letter

parts.note: stoor (stour) is a Scots word for tumult or commotion
B is the second grade, second class

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out around low-grade traffic lights in a South African city.
explanation.walkthrough: Durban is in South Africa, where traffic lights are called robots.
explanation.definitionFit: In South African English a robot is a set of traffic lights, so robots are the city's signals.

clue.text: Highest point reached by river in a long time, end of June

indicators.note: the river sits within the phrase for a long time

parts.note: a long time is an age
the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the last letter of June

explanation.surface: A river reaches its highest level after a long while, at the end of June.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the farthest point of an orbit from Earth, hence any climax or peak.

clue.text: Directly opposed cut that's overturned annual return

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
AR is the standard abbreviation for an annual return

explanation.surface: A company's annual filing has been rejected and cut, entirely contrary to what was wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar opposites lie at the two ends of an axis, so polar means diametrically opposed.

clue.text: Rare form of tree, impressive from below, dropping first of leaves

indicators.note: read from below in a down entry, the word comes backwards
dropping means letting go, so the chosen letter is removed

parts.note: noble in the sense of grand or impressive

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of leaves

explanation.surface: An unusual tree looks imposing from beneath once it sheds its leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed, the impressive word loses its L: ELBON becomes EBON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a rare, poetic form of the noun ebony, the dark-wooded tree.

clue.text: American mountain song about rambling Ed O'Kane?

indicators.note: about means around, so the song wraps round the jumbled name
rambling wanders aimlessly, so the name's letters stray into a new order

parts.note: the yodel is the Alpine herdsman's song
the seven letters of the name, rearranged

explanation.surface: An American's song about a wandering Irishman named Ed O'Kane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American mountain song' looks like one phrase for the definition, but only 'American' defines; the song famously named after the nickname is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee-Doodle is an old nickname for an American, taken from the Revolutionary-era song.

clue.text: Mixed up extremes of outrage I abhor in what drives Brexiteers

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of outrage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confused and outraged declares their loathing of whatever motivates Leave voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed up' reads as one phrase, but only 'Mixed' is the signal; 'up' joins the letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Europhobia is hostility to the European Union, the sentiment behind the campaign to leave it.

clue.text: Weak American son — what's he called?

definitions.note: a noun: a weakling, in American slang
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a feeble, timid person, in US slang
second meaning: a South Wales form of address for a lad or mate

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks the name of a feeble American's boy; the second half really asks what a young man is called in South Wales dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Wuss is US slang for a weakling, and in South Wales it is a familiar way of addressing a boy or pal.

clue.text: Primate's title, nuisance if back to front

indicators.note: with its back brought to the front, the last letter moves to the start of the word

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome nuisance

explanation.surface: An archbishop finds his formal title a nuisance when it gets reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' here is a single move, not a full reversal: the final E jumps to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebor, short for Latin Eboracum (York), is the signature of the Archbishop of York, Primate of England.

clue.text: Part of China, it briefly houses troops as winter quarters maybe

indicators.note: a building that houses people holds them inside, so the soldiers go within

parts.note: Canton is the old name for Guangzhou and its province
it shortened to 't, as in 'tis
troops are the men

explanation.surface: A Chinese region briefly quarters soldiers through the winter.
explanation.walkthrough: CANTON and T together house MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantonment is a set of military lodgings, such as quarters where troops spend the winter.

clue.text: Edmund's keen on being entry for medal

indicators.note: an entry goes into something, so this word is placed inside the medal

parts.note: BEM is the British Empire Medal
re means on or about

explanation.surface: A man called Edmund is eager to enter for a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund is Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet whose archaic words Chambers tags as Spenserian.
explanation.definitionFit: Breem is Spenser's spelling of breme, meaning fierce or sharp, hence keen.

clue.text: Melanesian canoe, number having replaced its centrepiece

indicators.note: the middle letter of the boat word is swapped out for the new one

parts.note: a kayak is a type of canoe
N is the algebraic symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A Melanesian's canoe has been given a new number painted across its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: N replaces the central Y of KAYAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Kanak is the name for an indigenous Melanesian of New Caledonia.

clue.text: Coarse linen cap mostly donned by our sailors

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
a cap donned sits on top, so in a down entry it comes above the sailors

parts.note: a hat with its last letter removed
the RN is Britain's Royal Navy

explanation.surface: British sailors wear caps made mostly of rough linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Harn is a Scots word for a coarse linen fabric.

clue.text: Region after renewing houses

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, running across its words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of after into renewing

explanation.surface: A district gets new homes after redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renewing' looks like an anagram signal, but nothing is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, terrene means the earth or a stretch of land, a tract or region.

clue.text: 'Bravo' some of the guests will be coming up with

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom, so the stretch runs backwards
some of a phrase is just a stretch of its letters

parts.note: a run inside the phrase, read backwards

explanation.surface: Some of the guests will call out 'Bravo'.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is tHE GUEsts, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Euge is a Latin exclamation of approval, 'well done!', used in English as a cry of applause.

clue.text: Close friend deserted by husband earlier bought provisions

indicators.note: when deserted the word is left without that letter, so it is removed

parts.note: Achates was the faithful companion of Aeneas, hence a loyal friend
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A close friend, abandoned by her husband, once bought supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier' marks the definition as obsolete English.
explanation.definitionFit: Acates is an obsolete word for purchased provisions, a source of the later word cates for delicacies.

clue.text: Popular outcry met EU falling out with English

indicators.note: a falling-out is a quarrel that breaks things up, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the five letters of met EU, rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Public uproar greets a meeting where the European Union fell out with the English.
explanation.definitionFit: An émeute, borrowed from French, is a riot or popular uprising.

clue.text: Pulling a face, having good liquor in unsuitable receptacle for it

indicators.note: the good liquor is placed within the receptacle

parts.note: a mug is the wrong vessel for spirits
G is the abbreviation for good
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces at being served fine spirits in a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For it' points back to the liquor: a mug is the wrong vessel for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug is to make exaggerated facial expressions, so mugging is grimacing or pulling faces.

clue.text: Pigment shade finally seen in earthenware pot

indicators.note: the letter appears within the pot word

parts.note: a cruse is a small earthenware jar

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of shade

explanation.surface: A shade of pigment has turned up inside a clay pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceruse is white lead, a pigment once used in paint and cosmetics.

clue.text: Swallow song that embodies extremes of longing, soaring

indicators.note: soaring rises, so in a down entry the letters read upwards
to embody is to hold within, so the song encloses those letters

parts.note: a tune is a song

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of longing

explanation.surface: A swallow's song is full of longing as it soars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, setting the scene of a soaring song, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Englut is an old verb meaning to gulp down or devour, to swallow.

clue.text: Deity celebrated with feast coming round

parts.note: sung in the sense of praised, as in sung by poets

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or feast

explanation.surface: A god is honoured with a festival that comes round each year.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun god is a deity personifying or ruling the sun, such as Ra or Helios.

clue.text: Flowering plant about lost in oblivion

indicators.note: the letter is lost from within the word, so it is removed

parts.note: silence in the sense of being forgotten, consigned to oblivion
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A flowering plant drifts into obscurity.
explanation.definitionFit: Silene is the genus of campions and catchflies, flowering plants of the pink family.

clue.text: O, no! King's scattered antelopes

indicators.note: scattered things are strewn about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters of O, no, king, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry of dismay as the king's herd of antelopes runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of King's is the verb 'is', not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The kongoni is the East African hartebeest; the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Architect for all to see occupying ceremonial seat

indicators.note: to occupy a seat is to sit within it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a gadi is the cushioned throne of an Indian ruler
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A famous architect sits on a grand throne in full public view.
explanation.walkthrough: A U-certificate film in Britain is suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoni Gaudí was the Catalan architect of the Sagrada Família in Barcelona.

clue.text: Young pigeon, one associated with Dagenham

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dialect word for a fledgling pigeon
second meaning: a member of the Dagenham Girl ...

explanation.walkthrough: Dagenham is a town in east London famous for its Girl Pipers, a bagpipe band.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word as a young pigeon, and the Dagenham Girl Pipers made its musician sense famous.

clue.text: Ruminant, very young one in NZ, entirely ecaudate

indicators.note: ecaudate means having no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: bub is Australian and New Zealand slang for a baby
all, without its tail

explanation.surface: A grazing animal, a newborn in New Zealand, has no tail at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The bubal is a North African hartebeest, an antelope and so a cud-chewing ruminant.

clue.text: Crow surrendering tail for coils of feathers, say

indicators.note: giving up its tail means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: A crow sheds its tail feathers in coils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' suggests the bird and its feathers, but it is the verb meaning to brag.
explanation.definitionFit: Boas are long fluffy scarves, often of feathers, coiled round the neck; snakes are the other kind, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Component of thing is motorized doohickey

indicators.note: a component is a part inside the whole, so the answer is a stretch within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of thing, all of is and the start of motorized

explanation.surface: A part of some motorised contraption is a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo, or gizmo, is an informal word for any gadget whose name escapes you, just like a doohickey.

clue.text: Good time away from work, sure to go for pottery stuff?

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: the letters are told to go, so they are removed from the word

parts.note: leisure is time off work
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: On a good day off, someone is set on doing some pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: the clay is potters' stuff only by suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Glei, or gley, is a sticky bluish-grey clay soil formed in waterlogged ground.

clue.text: Learner's gone into walker, it's alleged in court

indicators.note: to have gone into something is to be inside it

parts.note: ped is short for pedestrian
L is the learner plate

explanation.surface: Court allegations claim a learner driver drove into a pedestrian.
explanation.definitionFit: Pled is a past tense of plead, used of a case put forward or a claim made in court.

clue.text: Run out, one departs with duck — cuckoo!

parts.note: ro is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for run out
a means one
d is the timetable abbreviation for departs
the Indian runner is a breed of duck

explanation.surface: A batsman is run out and departs for a duck; a mad outcome!
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, which makes 'duck' look like O; here it is the duck breed. The exclamation mark tips off that 'cuckoo' is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is a fast-running bird of the American southwest belonging to the cuckoo family.

clue.text: Crumble made with fruit? Ties in when cooked with grain inside

indicators.note: the mixture sits inside the fruit word

parts.note: a date is a fruit

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
gr is the abbreviation for grain

explanation.surface: A recipe: a fruit crumble with oats or grain baked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumble' looks like the pudding, the picture the cooking words paint, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to break up into small pieces, as something crumbling does.
